case.title: Hostinger-themed Pages phishing infrastructure
case.boundary: Exact response hashes, stable code flow and repeated deployment naming support one maintained Hostinger-themed kit family. They do not establish victim count, successful credential submission, one operator, provider compromise or common ownership of every account and service.

nodes.label: 298 task-query Pages names
nodes.meaning: The exact URLScan task-hostname search returned 298 fixed-prefix Pages names. One more matching name appeared only through another pivot, producing a 299-name local union.

nodes.label: Cloned Hostinger login document
nodes.meaning: Archived HTML and screenshots preserved a localized Hostinger Mail clone with username and password fields. Five known hosts later served the same document bytes.

nodes.label: Exact credential-harvester core
nodes.meaning: The retained core reads email and password fields, Base64-encodes them, prepares a POST and presents the same fake error before redirecting to legitimate Hostinger Mail.

nodes.label: Separate Render credential receiver
nodes.meaning: The archived code names a separate Render service for fields ai, pr and pg. The investigation did not submit the form or contact the receiver.
nodes.confidence: direct code reference; receiver not contacted

nodes.label: Two versioned tracker modules
nodes.meaning: Legacy and current tracker hashes preserve nearly identical structure while changing their Render destination, supporting module lineage without identifying an operator.

nodes.label: 467 exact-core observations
nodes.meaning: The exact credential-core hash appeared in 467 URLScan observations across 262 task domains from December 2025 through August 2026. These are scan observations, not victims.

nodes.label: Maintained reusable phishing kit family
nodes.meaning: Stable credential code, cloned UI assets, versioned tracking, repeated query grammar and automated project naming support a maintained reusable kit-family assessment.
nodes.confidence: high for capability and code lineage

nodes.label: Victims, operator and provider accounts unknown
nodes.meaning: Public observations do not reveal successful submissions, victim count, provider-account ownership or whether one operator controlled every deployment. Hostinger is the impersonated brand; Cloudflare and Render are service platforms.
